subtopic: Geometry of Complex Numbers (Argand Geometry & Loci)
title: Lines, collinearity, and the perpendicular bisector

board_content.text: $z$ lies on the line through $z_1,z_2$ iff $\dfrac{z-z_1}{z_2-z_1}$ is real.
'Equidistant from two points' reads directly as the perpendicular bisector.
Translate words to a $z$-equation; that is the whole skill.

segments_english.text: Let's express straight-line conditions in the language of z. The recurring skill is translating a geometric sentence into a complex equation.
A point z lies on the line through z one and z two exactly when the ratio z minus z one, over z two minus z one, is a real number — because being on the line means zero turning.
Equivalently, that ratio equals its own conjugate, which is just the algebraic way of saying it's real.
The general equation of a line in this notation is a bar z, plus a z bar, plus b equals zero, where a is complex and b is real.
Collinearity is the same idea for three points: z one, z two, z three are collinear exactly when z three minus z one, over z two minus z one, is real — same direction, no turn.
Now the perpendicular bisector. The condition modulus of z minus z one equals modulus of z minus z two describes all points equidistant from z one and z two.
And equidistant from two fixed points is, word for word, the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them. Reading the words straight off gives the locus.
That's the whole skill of this subtopic: translate the geometric words into a z-equation, and translate a z-equation back into geometry.

segments_hinglish.text: Straight-line conditions ko z ki bhaasha mein express karte hain. Recurring skill hai ek geometric sentence ko complex equation mein translate karna.
Ek point z, z one aur z two se jaati line par tabhi hai jab ratio z minus z one, over z two minus z one, ek real number ho — kyunki line par hona matlab zero turning.
Equivalently, wo ratio apne hi conjugate ke barabar hai, jo bas real hone ka algebraic tareeka hai.
Is notation mein line ki general equation hai a bar z, plus a z bar, plus b barabar zero, jahan a complex hai aur b real.
Collinearity teen points ke liye wahi idea hai: z one, z two, z three collinear tabhi hain jab z three minus z one, over z two minus z one, real ho — same direction, koi turn nahi.
Ab perpendicular bisector. Condition modulus of z minus z one barabar modulus of z minus z two un saare points ko describe karti hai jo z one aur z two se equidistant hain.
Aur do fixed points se equidistant hona, shabd-ba-shabd, unhe jodne wale segment ka perpendicular bisector hai. Shabdon ko seedha padhne se locus mil jaata hai.
Yehi is subtopic ki poori skill hai: geometric words ko z-equation mein translate karo, aur z-equation ko wapas geometry mein.
